messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: PD#INC-4821 fired for service=private-controlplane-health — severity=high — symptom=controlplane-heartbeats-flapping

pd-bot: PagerDuty event: triggered by healthcheck-monitor (private-controlplane-nyc). Trigger detail: 'control-plane gRPC stream resets > 15% in 5m' — links: https://pd.example/INC-4821

sre-oncall: Acked oncall. I'm on it — starting triage. tagging eng-runtime and networking.

miguel: I'm seeing the same alerts in the controlplane logs. Multiple customer VPCs (cust-msk-01, cust-velvet-02) reporting TLS renegotiate and agent disconnects. Could be BGP/route flapping or NAT gateway churn.

alyssa: Noted. Customer impact? Any 5xx surface to hosted API or just private control plane heartbeats?

jordan: Quick check — private control plane metrics show short spikes in active stream resets and a correlated jump in egress RTT to customers in us-east-1. No downstream hosted-api 5xx so far. Customers report degraded sync (agent reconnects every ~15-60s).

kevin: Reproduced via packet capture from onprem-agent for cust-msk-01: seeing TCP RSTs mid-stream. Suspect an intermediate path device doing asymmetric routing failover.

alyssa: Ok, mitigation plan options: 1) Move affected control plane replicas for those customers to a different availability zone (quick restart, short window). 2) Temporarily route their control traffic via public control plane fallback (requires consent but fast). 3) Instruct customer to check on-prem firewall/NAT for conn tracking. Which do we prefer?

miguel: Recommend 2) public control plane fallback for immediate customer relief. I'll coordinate opt-in per customer (we have consent for cust-velvet-02 but need explicit for cust-msk-01). I'll draft messages.

jordan: I'll prepare the rollout: update routing policy for the two customer IDs to allow fallback, then monitor heartbeats for 10m. If stable, we keep fallback until root cause addressed.

sre-oncall: Actioning fallback for cust-velvet-02 now. command: ```sh
# route override for customer cust-velvet-02
redwoodctl controlplane route set --customer cust-velvet-02 --target public-fallback-us-east --reason "failover - PD INC-4821"
```

(sre-oncall): Applied. Watching metrics + logs. Heartbeats recovering for cust-velvet-02 (first successful reconnect at +28s).

miguel: Cust-msk-01 contacted; they gave approval to fail over. Proceeding to apply.

kevin: While that's rolling, I captured a snippet from tcpdump showing intermittent path MTU blackhole symptoms (ICMP fragmentation-needed seen). Paste: ```
12:23:44.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.443 > 172.20.0.10.53812: Flags [P.], seq 1:1370, ack 1, win 64240, length 1369
12:23:44.123789 IP 172.20.0.10 > 10.0.0.5: ICMP frag-needed, mtu 1400
```

alyssa: Interesting. That points at an intermediate device or misconfigured MTU on customer edge. Good to note in RCA. For now, fallback should mask the problem.

jordan: Routes applied for cust-msk-01. Both customers on public-fallback. Monitoring window started.

sre-oncall: Heartbeats normalized for both customers. I'll keep the channel open for 30m then hand off to the next oncall for follow-up and RCA.

miguel: I'll open a support ticket with both customers and include the packet captures + suggestion to verify MTU and middlebox behavior. Also filing internal ticket (ENG-priv-net-241) to triage persistent controlplane path selection and add better MTU fallbacks.

tara: Thanks team. I'll take the 30m watch and then own handoff. Next oncall is tara at 1968052200.

kevin: Quick followups to add to postmortem checklist: add explicit MTU detection in controlplane handshake, improve agent reconnect backoff jitter, and expose customer-level path metrics in console.

pd-bot: PagerDuty note: Incident INC-4821 acknowledged by sre-oncall. Escalation to eng-runtime on-call at +12m if not resolved.

tara: Logging final interim status: mitigated via public control plane fallback for affected customers. No widespread customer outage. Will coordinate with eng-runtime and cust success for communications. Creating a summary now and will attach logs for RCA. :white_check_mark:
